name: Delayed SEIR with Explicit Initial Cohort Histories
description: Illustrative fixed-duration delayed SEIR scenario with explicit uniform ages for the existing initial exposed and infectious cohorts. For t<0, the incubation outflow history is Initial Exposed/Tau E=20 people/day, and recovery-inflow history is Initial Infectious/Tau I=10/7 people/day. These histories correspond to exposure incidence 20/day on [-5,0) and 10/7 per day on [-12,-5); each integral equals its existing initial cohort. At t=0 the exposure law becomes beta*S*I/N. N is the actual conserved population sum 1000110, preserving all original initial stock values rather than claiming their sum is 1000000. Nested fixed-delay calls use distinct constant prehistories and left-continuous sampled history at nonnegative times. Full-horizon, refinement, population conservation, nonnegative age-window integrals, and boundary checks are retained. This is not the published Kiselev/BioUML model: that source uses weighted delayed stock terms, additional clinical compartments, instantaneous splitting and fitted country data. No epidemic forecast or empirical calibration is claimed.
reference: Kiselev et al. (2023), Scientific Reports 13:13439, doi:10.1038/s41598-023-40008-9 provides delay-model context; its weighted-stock-delay BioUML equations differ from this fixed-duration local scenario. Uniform initial cohort histories are explicit local model inputs, mathematically derived from existing E0=100,I0=10 and fixed durations 5,7.
